unterschrift.text: , White to move. The pawn on c5 and the knight on c6 attack the pawn on d4 (red arrows); the pawns on c3 and e3 and the knight on f3 defend it (gold arrows).

fragen.frage: Why doesn't White need to defend the pawn on d4 any further right now?
antworten: Two attackers face three defenders: capturing on d4 wins nothing.
The pawn on d4 is pinned to the king.
In the opening, Black is not allowed to capture pawns.
fragen.erklaerung: You count on the square: as long as the defenders are not fewer than the attackers, every capture on d4 ends in a mere exchange.

antworten: It threatens mate on f7 at once.
It develops a piece and prepares Nd5, which attacks the queen with tempo.

fragen.frage: Why doesn't it bother White that Black can capture the pawn on d4?
antworten: The lead in development is worth more than a pawn.
The pawn on d4 is defended three times.
After the capture, Black is mated at once.
fragen.erklaerung: White has a broad center and three developed pieces, and is about to castle. A pawn that Black grabs with further moves of the same pieces only makes this deficit bigger.

unterschrift.text: White has already castled, has brought the rook to the open e-file and is to move. The gray arrow shows the line of the pin: the black knight on e4 must not move, or its own king would be in check. The gold arrow shows the additional attack of the knight on c3 on exactly this square – the red square e4 shows that White wins the piece at once.

fragen.frage: Why is the black knight on e4 lost?
antworten: It has no free square left.
It is pinned to the king on e8 and attacked twice.
White threatens mate on e8.
fragen.erklaerung: The rook on e1 pins it to the king, and the knight on c3 attacks it as well. A king that stays in the middle too long is what makes such pins possible in the first place.

unterschrift.text: White to move. The gray arrow shows the obvious capture Nxc5. But the gold arrow shows the much stronger move: Nf6+ gives check to the king on e8 and at the same time attacks the queen on d5 (both red).

fragen.frage: Why is 1. Nf6+ stronger than 1. Nxc5?
antworten: It gives check and attacks the queen on d5 at the same time: White wins the queen.
It gives mate.
It protects White's own king.
fragen.erklaerung: If you look at the checks first, you find the fork. Nxc5 only trades knight for bishop.

unterschrift.text: – Black to move. The red square d3 shows the problem: there, White's own bishop has cut off the white queen's defense of d4. 3:3 has become 3:2.

fragen.frage: Why does Black capture on d4 now?
antworten: The pawn on d4 is pinned.
Otherwise White threatens mate.
Three attackers against two defenders: at the end of the exchange, a pawn is left over.
fragen.erklaerung: The count decides: with more attackers than defenders, the attacking side wins material.

fragen.frage: Why does Black play 7... Bd7 first instead of Nxd4 at once?
antworten: After Nxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4, Bb5+ clears the d-file, and the queen on d1 captures the queen on d4.
Bd7 prepares queenside castling.
Nxd4 would be a retreat.
fragen.erklaerung: Only Bd7 puts a bishop between b5 and the king. Then Bb5 is no longer check, and the threat against d4 becomes real.

abbildungen.unterabschnitt: One attacker is too few, three are enough: the Greek gift

unterschrift.text: The failed attempt. White to move. The bishop stands on e2, where of all things it blocks the d1–h5 diagonal (gray) that the queen would need to reach the kingside. White wants to attack with knight and queen – but only the knight on f3 even gets within reach. Red: the target h7.

fragen.frage: Why does the attack with 1. Ng5 fail?
antworten: The knight on g5 is lost at once.
The knight stays alone; the queen can't get to h5 because the bishop on e2 is in the way.
Black then gives mate.
fragen.erklaerung: An attack with one piece against a well-defended king fizzles out. Only superior force makes it dangerous.

abschnitt.label: sec:k1-angriff
abschnitt.titel: Attack needs superior force: the golden attack rule

abbildungen.unterabschnitt: One attacker is too few, three are enough: the Greek gift

unterschrift.text: This is how it should have looked. The bishop on d3 itself aims at h7 (gold arrow), the knight on f3 reaches g5 – and as soon as it does, the d1–h5 diagonal opens for the queen. Three attackers reach h7 (red) – and only the king itself defends the square.

antworten: The bishop can't be captured on h7.
Black has already castled and can no longer move the king.
Three attackers reach h7, and only the king defends: the superior force carries the sacrifice.
fragen.erklaerung: After Kxh7, Ng5+ and Qh5 bring the knight and queen in with tempo. Against three attackers, a single defender is not enough.
